query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount of Cr to single-phase fcc FeCoNi can overcome the coercivity limitation
generation.intervention: adding a small amount of Cr
generation.baseline: single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative
generation.uncertainty: uncertainty in the measurement of coercive field
generation.falsification_experiment: measure the coercive field of the Cr-modified alloy and compare it to the baseline

Question: How does the addition of Sn (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) affect the phase constitution, microstructure, and magnetic properties (specifically saturation magnetization, remanence, and Curie temperature) of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 high-entropy alloys?. System: FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10). Processing: Vacuum arc-melting of 99.99% purity constituent elements using a water-cooled Cu crucible, followed by suction casting into a 100 × 10× 2 mm water-cooled Cu mold after remelting four times.. Test conditions: XRD scan speed of 1°/min; VSM measurements at an applied magnetic field of 1 T; HCTS hysteresis curves using a 27 × 9 × 1.7 mm rectangular sample at a magnetic field of 25 kA/m; DSC thermal stability analysis at a heating rate of 10 K/min.. Findings: The ratio of I(110)BCC/I(111)FCC increases from 0.38 (x=0) to 10.53 (x=0.10), indicating a rapid increase in BCC phase content.; Saturation magnetization (Ms) increases from 78.6 Am2/kg to 88.8 Am2/kg as x increases f
